s: Reference price ₹1,209 (NSE close, 21 October 2026) · Approx. market cap ₹16.34 lakh crore · 52-week range ₹1,152–₹1,611
Latest published quarter: Q1 FY27. Reliance had not published September-quarter results on its investor site by the report date.
Reliance combines a large cash-generative O2C business with faster-growing digital, retail and media platforms. FY26
EBITDA rose 13.4% to ₹2.08 lakh crore; Jio Platforms EBITDA grew 18.8% and Retail 8%. Q1 FY27 recurring EBITDA rose
10.1%, led by Jio and O2C, while Retail EBITDA slipped 1.1% and group finance costs rose 18.5%. Jio Platforms’ proposed
IPO is a near-term value-discovery catalyst, but valuation, dilution and parent-level value realisation remain uncertain.
At ₹1,209, the share is close to its 52-week low and trades around 20.3x FY26 EPS of ₹59.7. Our base case uses FY27 EPS
of ₹66 and a 23.2x exit multiple. The resulting ₹1,531 value supports an Accumulate view, with medium conviction because of
O2C cyclicality and Retail margin execution.

FY26 PAT ₹95,754 crore (+17.8%); EPS ₹59.7 versus ₹51.5 in FY25. Capex ₹1,44,271 crore. At June 2026, net debt was
₹1,22,914 crore and net debt/LTM EBITDA 0.60x. CRISIL reaffirmed AAA/Stable in September 2026.
The prior-year base included a ₹8,924 crore listed-investment gain; company materials exclude it when discussing recurring
growth. Against the unadjusted base, EBITDA and PAT were lower. Segment EBITDA: O2C ₹17,010 crore (+17.2%); Digital
Services ₹21,255 crore (+16.1%); Retail ₹6,309 crore (-1.1%); Oil & Gas ₹4,973 crore (-0.5%).
Digital services. Jio Platforms’ Q1 EBITDA rose 15.1% to ₹20,865 crore, with a 53.3% margin. Subscriber scale, ARPU
progression, fixed broadband and 5G usage underpin the growth case. Increased finance costs following 5G asset
Jio listing. Jio Platforms filed its RHP on 14 October for a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares. The filing advances price
discovery but does not guarantee a valuation uplift for RIL shareholders. The offer price, dilution and use of proceeds matter.
Retail execution. Q1 gross revenue grew 7.4%, but EBITDA fell 1.1% and the margin declined 80 bps to 7.9%. Management
cited investment in digital commerce. Better operating leverage would lift earnings quality; continued margin erosion would
O2C and new energy. Q1 O2C benefited from sharp fuel-crack and downstream-delta increases, but under-recoveries,
SAED-related costs, crude premiums and logistics constrained margin capture. New energy projects carry long-term option
value; no separate value is assigned here until commercial returns are demonstrated.
Illustrative forward P/E method: FY27 EPS scenarios start from FY26 reported EPS of ₹59.7. These estimates are not
company guidance. A multiples-based approach is used because segment-level ownership, intra-group items and IPO price
discovery make an SOTP particularly assumption-sensitive.
Scenario weights: 25% bear / 50% base / 25% bull; probability-weighted fair value is approximately ₹1,517, rounded to
₹1,530. Reference price/FY26 EPS is 20.3x; base forward P/E is 18.3x. The average external analyst target is ₹1,666 across
25 analysts, but that snapshot was last updated 21 September and is not treated as current or independent valuation
The IMF’s October 2026 WEO projects 7% real GDP growth for India in 2026, supporting a constructive demand backdrop for
telecom and retail. Reliance remains exposed to imported crude and global petrochemical cycles.

3. Jio IPO: weak price discovery, dilution, delay or limited parent-level value realisation could disappoint.
4. Capex and capital allocation: high investment could slow deleveraging and free cash flow.

6. Conglomerate discount: cross-holdings and valuation complexity can limit re-rating.
